'''Philip N. Benfey''' (January 31, 1953 – September 26, 2023) was an American plant biologist renowned for his pioneering research in root biology, plant development, and genomics. He was a Distinguished Professor of Biology at [[Duke University]] making significant contributions to understanding the genetic and molecular basis of root growth and development. He was also known for his mentorship fostering the careers of numerous scientists worldwide....<ref name="NaturePlants2024">{{cite journal |last1=Birnbaum |first1=Kenneth |title=Philip Benfey (1953–2023) |journal=Nature Plants |volume=10 |issue=October |pages=1436–1438 |year=2024 |doi=10.1038/s41477-024-01789-7|pmid=39289549 |bibcode=2024NatPl..10.1436B }}</ref> His achievements  inspired the dedication of a lifetime achievement award in his name after he died <ref>{{cite web |title=Arabidopsis Community Lifetime Achievement Award Named to Honor Philip N. Benfey |url=https://www.arabidopsiscommunity.org/news-events/benfey-arabidopsis-community-lifetime-achievement-award|website=Arabidopsis Community Website |date=2024-04-11 |access-date=2024-10-23}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Philip Benfey was born in Bryn Mawr, Pennsylvania. He pursued early studies at the University of Paris VI, earning a DEUG diploma (Diplome d'Etudes Universitaire Generale). He later received his Ph.D. in cell and developmental biology from [[Harvard University]] under the guidance of Dr. [[Philip Leder]], focusing on immunology. After recognizing the potential for transgenics in plants, he undertook postdoctoral research at [[Rockefeller University]] in the lab of Dr. [[Nam-Hai Chua]], where he characterized the now widely-used cauliflower mosaic virus 35S promoter, advancing the study of gene regulation in plants.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Benfey |first1=PN |last2=Chua |first2=NH |title=The cauliflower mosaic virus 35S promoter: Combinatorial regulation of transcription in plants |journal=Science |volume=250 |pages=959–966 |year=1990 |issue=4983 |doi=10.1126/science.250.4983.959|pmid=17746920 |bibcode=1990Sci...250..959B }}</ref>

== Career and research ==
In 1991, Benfey joined the Department of Biology at [[New York University]] (NYU), where he became a full professor in 2001. At NYU, he founded the Center for Comparative [[Functional genomics|Functional Genomics]] and conducted fundamental research in the [[molecular genetics]] of root development. His early work focused on understanding asymmetric cell divisions in roots and led to the identification of key regulatory genes, such as SHORT-ROOT and SCARECROW, which are crucial for radial patterning in the model plant [[Arabidopsis thaliana]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Benfey |first1=PN |last2=Helariutta |first2=Y |title=SHORT-ROOT gene controls radial patterning of the Arabidopsis root through radial signaling |journal=Cell |volume=101 |pages=555–567 |year=2000 |issue=5 |doi=10.1016/s0092-8674(00)80865-x|pmid=10850497 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

In 2002, Benfey moved to [[Duke University]], where he was named the Paul Kramer Distinguished Professor of Biology and served as the department chair.<ref>{{cite web |title=Philip N. Benfey Named Fellow of AAAS |url=https://aspb.org/newsletter/archive/2011/julaug11.pdf |website=American Society of Plant Biologists Newsletter |date=2011-08-01 |access-date=2024-10-14}}</ref> He played a key role in establishing the Duke Center for [[Systems biology|Systems Biology]] and was its director from 2007 to 2013.<ref name="PNAS2023">{{cite journal |last1=Raikhel |first1=Natasha |last2=Ecker |first2=Joseph |last3=Coruzzi |first3=Gloria |title=Remembering Philip N. Benfey: A visionary pioneer in plant biology and mentor extraordinaire |journal=PNAS |volume=120 |issue=45 |year=2023 |doi=10.1073/pnas.2317677120|bibcode=2023PNAS..12017677R |pmc=10636296 }}</ref> His leadership emphasized interdisciplinary research, combining biology with mathematics, physics, and computational approaches to advance the study of plant systems biology.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Benfey |first1=PN |title=Taking a developmental perspective on systems biology |journal=Developmental Cell |volume=21 |issue=1 |pages=27–28 |year=2011 |doi=10.1016/j.devcel.2011.06.016|pmid=21763617 |pmc=3139400 }}</ref>

Benfey’s lab made significant advances in root biology, particularly through the development of innovative imaging techniques<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Busch |first1=W |last2=Benfey |first2=PN |title=A microfluidic device and computational platform for high-throughput live imaging of gene expression |journal=Nature Methods |volume=9 |issue=11 |pages=1101–1106 |year=2012 |doi=10.1038/nmeth.2185|pmid=23023597 |pmc=3492502 }}</ref> and the application of tissue specific<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Brady |first1=SM |last2=Benfey |first2=PN |title=A High-Resolution Root Spatiotemporal Map Reveals Dominant Expression Patterns |journal=Science |volume=318 |issue=5851 |pages=801–806 |year=2007 |doi=10.1126/science.1146265|pmid=17975066 |bibcode=2007Sci...318..801B }}</ref> and single-cell RNA sequencing <ref>{{cite journal |last1=Shahan |first1=Rachel |last2=Benfey |first2=PN |title= A single-cell Arabidopsis root atlas reveals developmental trajectories in wild-type and cell identity mutants. |journal=Developmental Cell |volume=57 |issue=4 |pages=543–560 |year=2022 |doi=10.1016/j.devcel.2022.01.008|pmid=35134336 |pmc=9014886 }}</ref> to create detailed maps of gene expression in plant roots. His team’s research revealed insights into how plants respond to environmental stressors and manage growth through coordinated gene expression networks<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Iyer-Pascuzzi |first1=Anjali |last2=Benfey |first2=PN |title= Cell identity regulators link development and stress responses in the Arabidopsis root. |journal=Developmental Cell |volume=21 |issue=4 |pages=770–782 |year=2011 |doi=10.1016/j.devcel.2011.09.009|pmid=22014526 |pmc=3204215 }}</ref>

Among innovations proposed by Benfey's lab are the following:

* Mobile transcription factors: Benfey’s research established the concept of mobile transcription factors that can specify asymmetric cell divisions in plant roots, leading to the discovery of key regulatory genes like SHORT-ROOT and SCARECROW.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Benfey |first1=PN |last2=Helariutta |first2=Y |title=SHORT-ROOT gene controls radial patterning of the Arabidopsis root through radial signaling |journal=Cell |volume=101 |pages=555–567 |year=2000 |issue=5 |doi=10.1016/s0092-8674(00)80865-x|pmid=10850497 |doi-access=free }}</ref>
* Technologies to study root growth and their underlying genetic and transcriptional programs : Benfey developed the RootArray, a microfluidic device allowing for the cultivation of multiple seedlings and detailed observation of root responses to environmental cues. This technology advanced the study of root system dynamics and paved the way for the founding of GrassRoots Biotechnology, which was later acquired by Monsanto.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Busch |first1=W |last2=Benfey |first2=PN |title=A microfluidic device and computational platform for high-throughput live imaging of gene expression |journal=Nature Methods |volume=9 |issue=11 |pages=1101–1106 |year=2012 |doi=10.1038/nmeth.2185|pmid=23023597 |pmc=3492502 }}</ref> He also developed several imaging technologies to study roots <ref>{{cite journal |last1=Rogers |first1=ED |last2=Monaenkova |first2=D |last3=Mijar |first3=M |last4=Nori |first4=A |last5=Goldman |first5=DI |last6=Benfey |first6=PN |title=X-Ray Computed Tomography Reveals the Response of Root System Architecture to Soil Texture |journal=Plant Physiology |volume=171 |issue=3 |pages=2028–2040 |doi=10.1104/pp.16.00397 |pmid=27208237 |pmc=4936573 |date=July 2016 |eissn=1532-2548}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Topp |first1=CN |last2=Iyer-Pascuzzi |first2=AS |last3=Anderson |first3=JT |last4=Lee |first4=CR |last5=Zurek |first5=PR |last6=Symonova |first6=O |last7=Zheng |first7=Y |last8=Bucksch |first8=A |last9=Mileyko |first9=Y |last10=Galkovskyi |first10=T |last11=Moore |first11=BT |last12=Harer |first12=J |last13=Edelsbrunner |first13=H |last14=Mitchell-Olds |first14=T |last15=Weitz |first15=JS |last16=Benfey |first16=PN |title=3D phenotyping and quantitative trait locus mapping identify core regions of the rice genome controlling root architecture |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America |volume=110 |issue=18 |pages=E1695–E1704 |doi=10.1073/pnas.1304354110 |pmid=23580618 |pmc=3645568 |date=April 30, 2013|doi-access=free |bibcode=2013PNAS..110E1695T }}</ref>
* Single-cell genomics: His lab was among the first to apply tissue-resolved and single-cell RNA sequencing to plant roots, revealing previously unknown aspects of root cell differentiation and gene expression.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Brady |first1=SM |last2=Benfey |first2=PN |title=A High-Resolution Root Spatiotemporal Map Reveals Dominant Expression Patterns |journal=Science |volume=318 |issue=5851 |pages=801–806 |year=2007 |doi=10.1126/science.1146265|pmid=17975066 |bibcode=2007Sci...318..801B }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Shahan |first1=Rachel |last2=Benfey |first2=PN |title= A single-cell Arabidopsis root atlas reveals developmental trajectories in wild-type and cell identity mutants. |journal=Developmental Cell |volume=57 |issue=4 |pages=543–560 |year=2022 |doi=10.1016/j.devcel.2022.01.008|pmid=35134336 |pmc=9014886 }}</ref>

== Professional recognition and leadership ==
Philip Benfey was an Investigator of the [[Howard Hughes Medical Institute]] (HHMI) from 2011 to 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Philip N. Benfey |url=https://www.hhmi.org/scientists/philip-n-benfey |website=Howard Hughes Medical Institute |access-date=November 1, 2024}}</ref> He was elected to the [[United States National Academy of Sciences]] in 2010 <ref>{{Cite web |title=Philip Benfey |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/philip-benfey-1q0f6a/ |website=National Academy of Sciences |access-date=November 1, 2024}}</ref> and became a Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] in 2004.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Philip N. Benfey |url=https://plantae.org/philip-n-benfey/ |website=Plantae |access-date=November 1, 2024}}</ref> In 2021, he was awarded the Pioneer Award from the [[American Society of Plant Biologists]] for his contributions to plant biology <ref>{{Cite web |title=Pioneer: Philip Benfey |url=https://aspb.org/membership/aspb-pioneer-members/pioneer-philip-benfey/#testimonials |website=American Society of Plant Biologists |access-date=November 1, 2024}}</ref>

Benfey served on numerous editorial boards, including ''Science'', ''PNAS'', and ''Developmental Cell''. He co-founded and chaired the Scientific Advisory Board at Hi Fidelity Genetics Inc., a company focused on improving crop performance through advanced breeding technologies.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Scientists Studying Roots to Help Crops |url=https://www.dtnpf.com/agriculture/web/ag/news/article/2019/05/01/scientists-studying-roots-help-crops |website=DTN Progressive Farmer |access-date=November 1, 2024}}</ref>
